scripts.content:
🎣 HOOK:

I gained 6 kilograms of pure muscle in 45 days using a method most trainers will never tell you about.

📝 CONTENT:

Here's what happened. I was stuck at 72 kilograms for 8 months. Lifting heavy, eating everything in sight, barely gaining 200 grams per week. Then my powerlifter friend told me something that changed everything.

Stop training like a bodybuilder if you want to gain muscle fast. Here's what I mean - most guys do 12 to 15 reps trying to feel the burn. That's endurance training disguised as muscle building.

I switched to the 3-6 rep range for compound movements only. Squats, deadlifts, bench press, overhead press. That's it. Three times per week, 45 minutes max. No bicep curls, no chest flys, no isolation work.

The reason this works is simple. Heavy compound movements trigger maximum muscle protein synthesis. Your body thinks it's under serious stress and responds by building muscle tissue fast.

But here's the secret part - I ate 4,200 calories daily with 180 grams of protein. Most guys eat 2,800 calories and wonder why they can't grow. You need fuel to build the machine.

I went from 72 kilograms to 78 kilograms in exactly 45 days. My bench press jumped from 85 kilograms to 102 kilograms.

Then I discovered something called "mechanical tension cycling" - and it changed everything. Here's how it works.

Most people train the same rep ranges every week. 8 to 12 reps, same weight, same routine. Your muscles adapt in 3 weeks and growth stops completely.

But here's what I did differently. Week one - heavy sets of 3 to 5 reps to build strength. Week two - moderate sets of 8 to 12 reps for hypertrophy. Week three - light sets of 15 to 20 reps for metabolic stress.

I also ate 2.2 grams of protein per kilo of body weight. That's 160 grams daily for me. Most guys eat maybe 80 grams and wonder why they can't gain muscle.

The result? I went from 73 kilos to 79 kilos in exactly 45 days. My bench press jumped from 80 kilos to 95 kilos.
